The '''Grinch''' is a character created by children's author and cartoonist [[Dr. Seuss]].<ref>{{Cite web|title=Who Was Dr. Seuss' Inspiration for the Grinch? Himself!|url=https://www.biography.com/news/dr-seuss-grinch-inspiration|last=Witter|first=Brad|website=Biography|access-date=2020-05-06}}</ref> He is best known as the titular main protagonist of the 1957 children's book ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas!]]'' He has been portrayed and voiced by many actors, including [[Boris Karloff]], [[Zero Mostel]], [[Hans Conried]], [[Bob Holt (actor)|Bob Holt]], [[Walter Matthau]], [[Anthony Asbury]], [[Jim Carrey]], [[Rik Mayall]], [[Benedict Cumberbatch]], [[Matthew Morrison]], [[David Howard Thornton]], and [[James Austin Johnson]].

==Character description==
The Grinch is depicted as a green, furry, pot-bellied, pear-shaped, snub-nosed [[humanoid]] creature with a cat-like face and a cynical personality. In full-color adaptations, he is typically colored green. He has spent the past 53 years living in seclusion on a cliff overlooking the town of [[Whoville]].

In contrast to the cheerful Whos, the Grinch is [[Misanthropy|misanthropic]], ill-natured, and mean-tempered. The reason for this is a source of speculation; the consensus among the Whos is that he was born with a heart that they say was "two sizes too small". Though always hateful, he especially hates the [[Christmas season]], making particular note of how disturbing the various elements of [[Christmas]] time are to him, including the earsplitting noises of strangely-designed musical instruments, eating [[Christmas dinner]], and singing [[Christmas carol]]s. Unable to stand the holiday any longer, he enacts a dastardly plan to stop it from happening.

Aided by his pet dog, Max, he meticulously designs a red suit to disguise himself as [[Santa Claus]] and breaks into the Whos' homes on [[Christmas Eve]] while they sleep to steal everything they own, and dump it off from a nearby mountain. Although he pulls off the theft successfully, on Christmas morning he is shocked to hear the Whos still singing cheerfully, happy simply to have each other. He then realizes that the holiday has a deeper meaning that he never considered. Inspired, he stops the Whos' belongings from falling off the edge of the mountain, and in the process his heart grows three times its size. He returns all the gifts he stole and gladly takes part in the Whos' Christmas celebration.

The Grinch is still portrayed as a bitter and ill-tempered character in artwork and other media. In both [[How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (TV special)|the animated TV special]] and [[How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000 film)|the 2000 live-action film]], he is shown to have superhuman strength when he stops an entire sleigh loaded with presents from going over a cliff and lifts it over his head, and he is also described as "[finding] the strength of ten Grinches plus two" during that moment of crisis. In the 2018 film, the Grinch has assistance saving all the Whos' stolen goods.

With the character's anti-Christmas spirit followed by the transformation on Christmas morning, scholars have noted similarity to [[Ebenezer Scrooge]] from [[Charles Dickens]]' 1843 novella ''[[A Christmas Carol]]''.<ref>{{cite book|first=Philip|last=Nel|author-link=Philip Nel|title=Dr. Seuss: American Icon|publisher=[[Continuum International Publishing Group]]|location=New York City|date=2003|page=130|isbn=978-0826417084}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|first=Jacob M.|last=Held|title=Dr. Seuss and Philosophy: Oh, the Thinks You Can Think|url=https://archive.org/details/drseussphilosoph00held|url-access=limited|publisher=[[Rowman & Littlefield]]|location=Lanham, Maryland|date=2011|isbn=978-1442203112|page=[https://archive.org/details/drseussphilosoph00held/page/n169 147]}}</ref> Cardiologist David Kass suggested that the growth of the Grinch's heart at the end of the story indicates that the Grinch has the physiology of a [[Burmese python]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Jon|last=Hamilton|url=https://www.npr.org/sections/health-shots/2017/12/22/571998558/heart-2-sizes-too-small-mr-grinch-see-your-cardiologist|title=Heart 2 Sizes Too Small? Mr. Grinch, See Your Cardiologist|website=[[NPR]]|date=December 22, 2017|access-date=December 22, 2017}}</ref>

In Seuss' book, the Grinch's hatred for Christmas is unknown, but the 2000 film adaptation provides a backstory in his upbringing: abandoned in infancy in Whoville and left in the cold, unnoticed by the revelers at a Christmas party, the Grinch is taken in by two Who women. He proves an unruly schoolboy and is bullied by a schoolmate, Augustus May Who (later Whoville's mayor), but falls for a Who girl named Martha May Whovier. Determined to impress her, he uses various family heirlooms to make an angel Christmas tree-topper for a Christmas gift exchange and vainly attempts to shave. He is mocked for his efforts by everyone at school except Martha and so conceives an abiding resentment. The TV special ''[[The Grinch Grinches the Cat in the Hat]]'' lays much of the blame on the absence of the Grinch's mother, who had been a positive, nurturing influence on the Grinch in her lifetime but died some time prior; when the Grinch is finally provoked to grieve at the end of that special, he returns to being good.

==History==
[[File:Ted Geisel NYWTS.jpg|thumb|left|Dr. Seuss is working on ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas!]]'' in early 1957]]
The first use of the word 'Grinch' in a work by Dr. Seuss appears in the 1953 book ''[[Scrambled Eggs Super!]]'' (one of the books withdrawn from circulation by the Seuss estate in 2021<ref>{{cite news|first1=Amanda|last1=Watts|last2=Asmelash|first2=Leah|title=6 Dr. Seuss books won't be published anymore because they portray people in 'hurtful and wrong' ways|url=https://www.cnn.com/2021/03/02/us/dr-seuss-books-cease-publication-trnd/index.html|date=March 2, 2021|work=CNN|access-date=March 2, 2021}}</ref>) about Peter T. Hooper, a boy who collects eggs from a number of exotic birds to make scrambled eggs. One of these exotic birds is the "Beagle-Beaked-Bald-Headed Grinch" who shares the later Grinch's cantankerous attitude.

The name later appeared in the May 1955 issue of ''[[Redbook]]'' in a 32-line poem called, "The Hoobub and the Grinch". This version bears virtually no resemblance to the later character other than name, instead being a fast-talking salesman in the vein of Sylvester McMonkey McBean from ''[[The Sneetches and Other Stories|The Sneetches]]'' and the Once-ler from Seuss's later book ''[[The Lorax]]''.<ref>{{cite book|title=Dr. Seuss: American Icon|author=Philip Nel|publisher=The Continuum International Publishing Group|year=2005|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=IjvHQsCn_pgC&q=%22The+Hoobub+and+the+Grinch%22|page=117|isbn=9780826417084}}</ref> "The Hoobub and the Grinch" would be republished as part of the posthumous anthology ''[[Horton and the Kwuggerbug and More Lost Stories]]'' in 2014, in which the illustration draws this Grinch far differently.<ref name=NPR>{{cite news|last1=Migaki|first1=Lauren|title=Horton Meets A... Who?|url=https://www.npr.org/2014/09/08/345880696/horton-meets-a-who-introducing-the-kwuggerbug-from-seuss-lost-stories|access-date=12 March 2015|publisher=[[NPR]]|date=8 September 2014}}</ref>

The Grinch, in his best known incarnation, made his book debut in the 1957 story ''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!'', written and illustrated by Dr. Seuss, published as both a [[Random House]] book and in an issue of ''Redbook'' magazine. In 1966, the story was adapted into an animated [[How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (TV special)|television featurette of the same name]], which was directed by [[Chuck Jones]] and included the song "[[You're a Mean One, Mr. Grinch]]". [[Boris Karloff]] serves as both the story's narrator and the voice of the Grinch, but the song was sung by [[Thurl Ravenscroft]], as Karloff could not sing.<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2005/12/25/magazine/25raven.html|title=Our Cereal Hero|access-date=December 27, 2009|work=[[The New York Times]]|first=Elizabeth|last=McCracken|date=December 25, 2005|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121115150612/http://www.nytimes.com/2005/12/25/magazine/25raven.html|archive-date=November 15, 2012|df=mdy-all}}</ref> The Grinch's green color debuted in the television special as a consensus choice among Jones and Seuss, who agreed green was the only choice that made sense.<ref name=":1">{{cite news|title='How the Grinch Stole Christmas'– Best Villain Since Old 'Scrooge!'|url=https://www.newspapers.com/image/496698273/?terms=how%20the%20grinch%20stole%20christmas&match=1|date=December 7, 1966|pages=17|work=[[Daily Record (New Jersey)|The Daily Record]]|access-date=December 11, 2023}}</ref>

In 1977, Seuss responded to the fan request for more Grinch tales by writing the animated television special ''[[Halloween Is Grinch Night]]''. The Grinch is voiced by [[Hans Conried]].<ref name="Woolery1">{{cite book|last=Woolery|first=George W.|title=Animated TV Specials: The Complete Directory to the First Twenty-Five Years, 1962-1987|date=1989|publisher=Scarecrow Press|isbn=0-8108-2198-2|access-date=March 27, 2020|url=https://archive.org/details/animatedtvspecia0000wool/page/118/mode/2up|pages=119–120}}</ref> This was followed in 1982, when [[Marvel Productions|Marvel]] green-lit ''[[The Grinch Grinches the Cat in the Hat]]'', a TV film co-starring [[The Cat in the Hat (character)|the Cat in the Hat]]. The Grinch is voiced by [[Bob Holt (actor)|Bob Holt]]. The special was produced by Dr. Seuss (though under his real name, Ted Geisel). Although not as successful as the original, the two films both received [[Emmy Awards]].<ref name="Woolery2">{{cite book|last=Woolery|first=George W.|title=Animated TV Specials: The Complete Directory to the First Twenty-Five Years, 1962-1987|date=1989|publisher=Scarecrow Press|isbn=0-8108-2198-2|access-date=March 27, 2020|url=https://archive.org/details/animatedtvspecia0000wool/page/124/mode/2up|pages=125–126}}</ref>

Several episodes of the 1996 [[Nick Jr. Channel]] television show ''[[The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss]]'' feature the Grinch as the main antagonist, this time in puppet form.<ref>{{cite web|title=The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss|url=https://www.henson.com/wubbulous-world-dr-seuss.php|publisher=The Jim Henson Company|access-date=December 22, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171223102055/https://www.henson.com/wubbulous-world-dr-seuss.php|archive-date=December 23, 2017}}</ref> He was performed and voiced by [[Anthony Asbury]] from Season 1 (1996) to Season 2 (1998).<ref name="Wubbulous">{{cite web|url=https://www.behindthevoiceactors.com/tv-shows/The-Wubbulous-World-of-Dr-Seuss/|title=The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss|website=Behind The Voice Actors|language=en-US|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref>

[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000 film)|A 2000 live-action feature musical comedy film based on the story]], directed by [[Ron Howard]] and starring [[Jim Carrey]] as the Grinch, was a major success at the box office.<ref name="Cinema Dave">{{cite book|last=Montalbano|first=Dave|title=The Adventures of Cinema Dave in the Florida Motion Picture World|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=hvfExNxOXpsC&pg=PA268|date=December 22, 2010|page=268|publisher=Montalbano Publishing|isbn=9781462836734|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Wonderful Christmas">{{cite book|last=Rowan|first=Terry|title=Having a Wonderful Christmas Time Film Guide|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=AzuyCQAAQBAJ&pg=PA70|date=April 27, 2014|page=70|publisher=Rowan Publishing|isbn=9781312140455|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref><ref name="RTGrinch">{{cite web|url=https://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=grinch.htm|title=How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000)|website=Box Office Mojo|access-date=July 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150310001717/http://boxofficemojo.com/movies/?id=grinch.htm|archive-date=March 10, 2015}}</ref> A video game based on the film, simply entitled ''[[The Grinch (video game)|The Grinch]]'', was released on several consoles and PC in the same year. It was followed in 2007 by the release of the [[Nintendo DS]] title ''[[Dr. Seuss: How the Grinch Stole Christmas!]]''.

The Grinch was portrayed on the stage when the story was turned into [[Dr. Seuss' How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (musical)|a 1994 musical]] by the Children's Theater Company out of [[Minneapolis]]. The show made it to [[Broadway theatre|Broadway]] by way of a limited run in 2006.<ref name="Fee">{{cite book|editor1-first=Christopher R.|editor1-last=Fee|editor2-first=Jeffrey B.|editor2-last=Webb|chapter-url=https://books.google.com/books?id=kXnEDAAAQBAJ&q=grinch+culture+of+the+united+states&pg=PA848|title=American Myths, Legends, and Tall Tales: An Encyclopedia of American Folklore|chapter=Santa Claus|publisher=[[ABC-CLIO]]|location=Santa Barbara, California|date=2016|access-date=December 22, 2017|isbn=9781610695688|page=848|via=[[Google Books]]}}</ref> Icelandic actor [[Stefán Karl Stefánsson]] portrayed the Grinch in the touring production of the musical from 2008 to 2015.<ref name="Grinch Tour">{{cite news|last=Gans|first=Andrew|title=Karl, Charles, Keenan-Bolger and More Cast in Grinch Tour|url=http://www.playbill.com/news/article/122048.html|date=October 6, 2008|publisher=Playbill|access-date=December 6, 2025|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081009025900/http://www.playbill.com/news/article/122048.html|archive-date=October 9, 2008}}</ref><ref name="Lloyd Grinch">{{cite news|last=Ng|first=David|title=Christopher Lloyd withdraws from 'Grinch' at the Pantages|url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/blogs/culture-monster-blog/story/2009-10-27/christopher-lloyd-withdraws-from-grinch-at-the-pantages|date=October 27, 2009|website=Los Angeles Times|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref><ref name="Karl Grinch">{{cite news|last=Lewis|first=Jessica|title=Christopher Lloyd Bows Out of LA's 'Grinch'; Replaced by Stefan Karl|url=https://www.broadwayworld.com/los-angeles/article/Christopher-Lloyd-Bows-Out-of-LAs-GRINCH-Replaced-by-Stefan-Karl-20091028|date=October 28, 2009|publisher=BroadwayWorld|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref> The Grinch is also a minor character in the 2000 musical ''[[Seussical]]'', which is based on multiple Seuss works.

The Grinch's story was adapted for [[The Grinch (film)|a 2018 animated film]] by [[Illumination (company)|Illumination Entertainment]], starring [[Benedict Cumberbatch]] as the title character.<ref name="Cumberbatch">{{cite news|last=Franich|first=Darren|title=Benedict Cumberbatch is the new Grinch|url=https://ew.com/article/2016/04/13/grinch-benedict-cumberbatch/|date=April 13, 2016|publisher=Entertainment Weekly|access-date=December 22, 2017}}</ref>

On December 9, 2020, [[NBC]] aired the holiday live production, ''[[Dr. Seuss' The Grinch Musical Live!]]'', based on the Broadway stage musical. [[Booboo Stewart]] plays young Max, Amelia Minto plays [[Cindy Lou Who]], [[Denis O'Hare]] plays old Max and [[Matthew Morrison]] stars as the Grinch. The musical includes songs from the original musical, such as "[[You're a Mean One, Mr. Grinch]]".<ref name="MusicLive1">{{cite news|last=Weisholtz|first=Drew|title=NBC bringing 'The Grinch' to life in new musical holiday special|url=https://www.today.com/popculture/nbc-bringing-grinch-life-new-musical-holiday-special-t198362|date=November 10, 2020|website=TODAY.com|language=en|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref><ref name="MusicLive2">{{cite news|last=Meyer|first=Dan|title=Dr. Seuss' The Grinch Musical Special, Starring Matthew Morrison, Airs on NBC December 9|url=https://www.playbill.com/article/dr-seuss-the-grinch-musical-special-starring-matthew-morrison-airs-on-nbc-december-9|date=December 9, 2020|publisher=Playbill|access-date=9 December 2020}}</ref><ref name="MusicLive3">{{cite news|last=Scribner|first=Herb|title='Dr. Seuss' The Grinch Musical!': Here's what we know so far|url=https://www.deseret.com/platform/amp/entertainment/2020/12/9/22165425/dr-seuss-the-grinch-musical-watch-stream-cast-details|date=December 9, 2020|website=Deseret News|access-date=December 9, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211221085152/https://www.deseret.com/platform/amp/entertainment/2020/12/9/22165425/dr-seuss-the-grinch-musical-watch-stream-cast-details|archive-date=December 21, 2021}}</ref>

In 2023, [[Outright Games]] and Casual Brothers Ltd. developed and released a video game titled ''The Grinch: Christmas Adventures'', in which you play as both the Grinch and his dog Max as they traverse through 18 levels in Whoville to steal Christmas presents from the Whos, including jigsaw puzzles in order to unlock upgrades.{{citation needed|date=March 2026}}

==Voice actors and portrayals==
[[File:Grinch iterations.png|thumb|Various iterations of the Grinch in other media.]]
In many different movies, specials, video games, commercials and television series, the Grinch has been voiced and played by many different actors throughout many films. In [[Chuck Jones]]' [[How the Grinch Stole Christmas! (TV special)|1966 television special]], the Grinch was voiced by [[Boris Karloff]] before he died three years later in 1969.<ref name="Karloff">{{cite news|last=Higgins|first=Bill|title=Hollywood Flashback: Boris Karloff Played His Final Creature in 1966's 'Grinch'|url=https://www.hollywoodreporter.com/news/general-news/boris-karloff-played-his-final-creature-1966s-grinch-1158086/|date=2018-11-08|website=The Hollywood Reporter|language=en-US|access-date=September 9, 2023}}</ref> [[Zero Mostel]] voiced the Grinch in the 1975 audio recording of ''How the Grinch Stole Christmas!'',<ref name="Mostel">{{cite book|last=Lindemann|first=Richard|title=The Dr. Seuss Catalog: An Annotated Guide to Works by Theodor Geisel in All Media, Writings About Him, and Appearances of Characters and Places in the Books, Stories and Films|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tLvABgAAQBAJ&pg=PA139|date=February 28, 2005|publisher=McFarland & Company|page=139|isbn=978-0786422234|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref> while [[Hans Conried]] voiced the character in ''[[Halloween Is Grinch Night]]''<ref name="Woolery1"/> and [[Bob Holt (actor)|Bob Holt]] voiced the character in ''[[The Grinch Grinches the Cat in the Hat]]'', a crossover with one of [[Dr. Seuss]]' characters [[The Cat in the Hat]].<ref name="Woolery2"/>

[[Walter Matthau]] voiced the character in ''Random House Home Video''.<ref name="Matthau">{{cite book|last=Lindemann|first=Richard|title=The Dr. Seuss Catalog: An Annotated Guide to Works by Theodor Geisel in All Media, Writings About Him, and Appearances of Characters and Places in the Books, Stories and Films|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=tLvABgAAQBAJ&pg=PA125|date=February 28, 2005|publisher=McFarland & Company|page=125|isbn=978-0786422234|access-date=December 6, 2025}}</ref> ''[[The Wubbulous World of Dr. Seuss]]'' also features the Grinch, where he was played by puppeteer [[Anthony Asbury]].<ref name="Wubbulous"/>[[File:USH Studio Tour Ride- Grinch.JPG|thumb|Set of the 2000 film ''How the Grinch Stole Christmas''|left]]The Grinch was voiced by [[Corey Burton]] in [[Seuss Landing]] and ''Sneech Beach Area''.<ref name="Corey Burton">{{cite web|title=Corey Burton – Islands of Adventure|url=http://www.coreyburton.com/ioa.html|access-date=April 25, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180405194601/http://www.coreyburton.com/ioa.html|archive-date=April 5, 2018}}</ref> In [[Ron Howard]]'s 2000 ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas (2000 film)|How the Grinch Stole Christmas]]'' film, the Grinch's first live-action feature, he was played by [[Jim Carrey]]. ==In popular culture==
{{in popular culture|date=December 2025}}
The Grinch has become an anti-icon of Christmas and the winter holidays, as a symbol of those who despise the holiday, much in the same nature as the earlier character of [[Ebenezer Scrooge]]. Over the years, the Grinch has appeared on various forms of memorabilia such as [[Christmas ornaments]], plush dolls, and various clothing items.<ref name="Fee" /> The grumpy, anti-holiday spirit of the character has led to the everyday term "Grinch"<ref name="TV Guide Book of Lists">{{cite book|title=TV Guide Book of Lists|url=https://archive.org/details/tvguidebookoflis0000unse|url-access=registration|date=2007|publisher=Running Press|location=Philadelphia, Pennsylvania|isbn=978-0-7624-3007-9|page=[https://archive.org/details/tvguidebookoflis0000unse/page/158 158]}}</ref><ref name="by Serf_12 December 17, 2009 7:21 PM EST">{{cite news|last=Schlesinger|first=Jill|title=Citigroup Suspends Foreclosures|url=http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-503983_162-5990467-503983.html|date=December 17, 2009|publisher=[[CBS Studios International]]|location=New York City|access-date=July 7, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101026130410/http://www.cbsnews.com/8301-503983_162-5990467-503983.html|archive-date=October 26, 2010}}</ref> coming to refer to a person opposed to [[Christmas and holiday season|Christmas time]] celebrations<ref>{{cite news|last=Curtis|first=Henry Pierson|url=https://www.palmbeachpost.com/article/20120331/NEWS/303316012|title=Orlando Grinch? Former Osceola County courts supervisor faces trial|date=March 31, 2012|newspaper=[[Palm Beach Post]]|publisher=[[GateHouse Media]]|location=Palm Beach, Florida|access-date=November 22, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181123111949/https://www.palmbeachpost.com/article/20120331/NEWS/303316012|archive-date=November 23, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Felps|first=Bruce|url=http://www.nbcdfw.com/news/local-beat/Grinch-Grabs-Salvation-Army-Kettle-106967863.html|title=Grinch Grabs Salvation Army Kettle|date=November 9, 2010|website=NBC 5 Dallas-Fort Worth|publisher=[[NBCUniversal]]|location=Dallas, Texas|access-date=July 7, 2012}}</ref> or to someone with a coarse, greedy attitude.<ref name="by Serf_12 December 17, 2009 7:21 PM EST"/> In 2002, ''[[TV Guide]]'' ranked The Grinch number 5 on its "50 Greatest Cartoon Characters of All Time" list.<ref name="TV Guide Book of Lists"/>

They had attempted to do this, unsuccessfully, for several Christmases.<ref>{{cite news|last=Busby|first=Mattha|title=Pranksters dress Angel of the North in Santa hat|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/dec/24/pranksters-angel-of-the-north-santa-hat-christmas-gateshead|newspaper=The Guardian|date=24 December 2018|access-date=December 29, 2018}}</ref> In the early hours of December 29, the pranksters returned, one of them dressed as the Grinch and the others as Santa Claus, and the Grinch "stole" Santa's hat.<ref>{{cite news|last=Busby|first=Mattha|title=The Grinch steals Santa hat from Angel of the North|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2018/dec/29/the-grinch-steals-santa-hat-from-angel-of-the-north|date=29 December 2018|newspaper=The Guardian|access-date=December 29, 2018}}</ref>

Starting in 2021, a popular meme depicted a blue version of the Grinch (known as "The Blinch") smiling, with text stating that his smile was a result of having "knee surgery tomorrow". The meme gained increased popularity in 2024.<ref>{{cite news|last=Notopoulos|first=Katie|title=Explaining the Grinch 'Knee Surgery is Tomorrow' meme|url=https://www.businessinsider.com/grinch-knee-surgery-is-tomrorow-meme-explained-2024-12|date=December 3, 2024|newspaper=The Business Insider|access-date=December 5, 2024}}</ref>

== In politics ==
Multiple politicians in the [[United Kingdom]] and the [[United States]] have been compared to the Grinch, often due to accusations that they will "steal" Christmas.

[[Sean Hannity]] and [[Laura Ingraham]] described then-president [[Joe Biden]] as "the Grinch Who Stole Christmas" on [[Fox News]] in 2021, criticizing him for delays in the supply chain for US imports.<ref>{{cite news|last=Ecarma|first=Caleb|title=Fox News Is Casting Joe Biden as the Grinch in This Year's Rendition of the "War on Christmas"|url=https://www.vanityfair.com/news/2021/10/10/fox-news-joe-biden-war-on-christmas|date=October 14, 2021|website=[[Vanity Fair (magazine)|Vanity Fair]]|language=en-US|access-date=December 23, 2023}}</ref>

[[Mick Lynch (trade unionist)|Mick Lynch]], former head of the UK's [[National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers]], was compared to the Grinch from November to December 2022 in media coverage of the ongoing [[2022–2023 United Kingdom railway strikes|railway strikes]] by the union. Tabloid newspaper ''[[Metro (British newspaper)|Metro]]'' as well as Prime Minister [[Rishi Sunak]] likened him to the Grinch and accused him of wanting to "steal Christmas". Lynch retorted that "I'm not the Grinch, I'm a trade union official and I'm determined to get a deal."<ref>{{cite news|last=Calvert|first=Alana|title=Sunak accused of 'playing the man, not the ball' after branding union boss 'Grinch'|url=https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/politics/rishi-sunak-mick-lynch-grinch-b2247475.html|date=19 December 2022|website=[[The Independent]]|language=en|access-date=December 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Solomons|first=Adam|title=Sunak brands union leader Lynch 'the Grinch'|url=https://www.lbc.co.uk/news/rishi-sunak-mick-lynch-rmt-rail-strikes-christmas-grinch/|date=17 December 2022|website=[[LBC]]|language=en|access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Nevett|first=Joshua|title=Mick Lynch: Union leader who's in the national spotlight|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-politics-63947584|date=13 December 2022|work=BBC News|language=en-GB|access-date=September 13, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title='I'm not the Grinch': RMT union boss Mick Lynch defends new Christmas and New Year strikes|url=https://news.sky.com/story/im-not-the-grinch-rmt-union-boss-mick-lynch-defends-new-christmas-and-new-year-strikes-12753543|date=23 November 2022|website=[[Sky News]]|language=en|access-date=December 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last1=Adu|first1=Aletha|last2=Middleton|first2=Joe|title='I'm not the Grinch': Mick Lynch defends Christmas rail strikes as talks called|url=https://www.theguardian.com/uk-news/2022/nov/23/ministers-talks-rail-union-leaders-christmas-strikes|date=November 23, 2022|work=[[The Guardian]]|language=en-GB|access-date=December 23, 2023|issn=0261-3077}}</ref>

In December 2023, lawyers for [[Donald Trump]] called [[special counsel]] [[Jack Smith (lawyer)|Jack Smith]] a Grinch in a court filing in response to Smith's request for an expedited appeal on whether Trump could claim [[Presidential immunity in the United States|presidential immunity]]. The filing directly quoted ''[[How the Grinch Stole Christmas!]]'', arguing that if the [[United States Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit|US Court of Appeals for the District of Columbia Circuit]] did not rule against Smith's request, it "would make President Trump's opening brief due the day after Christmas. This proposed schedule would require attorneys and support staff to work round-the-clock through the holidays, inevitably disrupting family and travel plans. It is as if the Special Counsel 'growled, with his Grinch fingers nervously drumming, "I must find some way to keep Christmas from coming. … But how?"'"<ref>{{cite news|last1=Barnes|first1=Daniel|last2=Gregorian|first2=Dareh|title=You're a mean one, Mr. Smith: Trump attorneys call special counsel the Grinch in court filing|url=https://www.nbcnews.com/politics/donald-trump/trump-attorneys-call-special-counsel-grinch-court-filing-rcna129548|date=December 13, 2023|website=[[NBC News]]|language=en|access-date=December 23, 2023}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Rabinowitz|first=Hannah|title=Trump lawyers say special counsel is a Grinch who would ruin holidays for attorneys {{!}} CNN Politics|url=https://www.cnn.com/2023/12/13/politics/the-grinch-trump-jack-smith/index.html|date=December 13, 2023|website=[[CNN]]|language=en|access-date=December 23, 2023}}</ref>

[[Image:ForgedFaun.jpg|thumb|right|240px|''The Faun'']]'''''The Faun''''' is a [[sculpture]] by British [[forger]] [[Shaun Greenhalgh]]. He successfully passed it off as a work by [[Paul Gauguin]], selling it at [[Sotheby's]] for £20,700 in 1994. Three years later, in 1997, it was bought by the [[Art Institute of Chicago]] for an undisclosed sum, thought to be about $125,000. It was hailed by them as "one of its most important acquisitions in the last twenty years."<ref name="theartnewspaper.com">Bailey, Martin (December 12, 2007). [https://web.archive.org/web/20071215015730/http://www.theartnewspaper.com/article.asp?id=7105 "Revealed: Art Institute of Chicago Gauguin sculpture is fake"]. ''The Art Newspaper''. December 12, 2007. Archived from [http://www.theartnewspaper.com/article.asp?id=7105 the original] on December 15, 2007.</ref>

For a decade the sculpture remained on display, and was part of a major joint exhibition on Gauguin with the [[van Gogh Museum]] in [[Amsterdam]]. However, following revelations about its existence at Greenhalgh's trial in 2007, ''The Faun'' was tracked down by ''[[The Art Newspaper]]'' to [[Chicago]] and exposed as a fake.

In October 2007, the Art Institute removed the statue from display, and announced that it was seeking [[damages|compensation]] from Sotheby's. What the ultimate fate of ''The Faun'' is to be has not yet been revealed.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/><ref name="nytimes.com">Vogel, Carol (December 13, 2007). [https://www.nytimes.com/2007/12/13/arts/13gauguin.html?_r=2&ref=arts&oref=slogin&oref=slogin "Work Believed a Gauguin Turns Out to Be a Forgery"]. ''New York Times''. Accessed December 14, 2007.</ref>

==Background to the forgery==
In the early to mid 1990s, Shaun Greenhalgh was predominately involved with paintings. He sold a [[Samuel Peploe]], but in particular he was successful with his [[Thomas Moran]]s. He sold one to [[Bolton Museum]] in 1994 and at [[New York City]] auctions in 1995 he sold seven, and is reckoned to have produced as many as 40.<ref>[http://www.boltonmuseums.org.uk/news/amarna-princess-statement "Amarna Princess statement"] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20081120062143/http://www.boltonmuseums.org.uk/news/amarna-princess-statement |date=November 20, 2008 }}. Bolton Museum. November 29, 2007.</ref><ref>Milmo, Cahal (November 17, 2007). [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/crime/family-of-forgers-fooled-art-world-with-array-of-finely-crafted-fakes-400718.html "Family of forgers fooled art world with array of finely crafted fakes"]. ''Independent''.</ref><ref name=chadwick/> Yet at the same time, he must have been researching the possibility of at least one Gauguin work. As well as ''The Faun'', he is known to have also forged a Gauguin vase, possibly at a later date.<ref>Lovell, Jeremy (November 17, 2007). [http://www.nzherald.co.nz/section/2/story.cfm?c_id=2&objectid=10476643 "Octogenerian British art forger sentenced"]. ''New Zealand Herald''. Accessed December 26, 2007.</ref>

Gauguin is significantly less well regarded for his sculptures than for his paintings. It is likely that Greenhalgh was aware of that, and saw it as an opportunity. Forgers typically focus on the lower priced artworks of major artists, for though they offer fewer returns, they are subject to much less scrutiny.<ref>Thompson, Clive. [http://nymag.com/nymetro/arts/features/9179/. "How to make a fake"], ''New York Magazine'', May 24, 2004. Accessed December 26, 2007.</ref> Moreover, Gauguin had left just enough of a record to indicate he may have been interested in producing such an item, a drawing of a [[faun]] sculpture in a [[sketchbook]] from 1887. This was backed up by suggestive historical events: at a Gauguin exhibition in 1906, a "faun [[ceramic art|ceramic]]" was displayed,<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake"/> and another listing for a work entitled "Faun" was found for a 1917 Nunes and Fiquet gallery exhibition.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> Scholars in the 1960s dutifully recorded these possibilities. Even in 2007, experts were still uncertain about how many ceramic sculptures Gauguin had actually produced. Estimates range from 55 to 80.<ref name="nytimes.com"/> Of these, between 30 and 60 are thought to be lost or destroyed.<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake">Storch, Charles; Artner, Alan (December 21, 2007). [http://www.latimes.com/entertainment/la-et-gauguin21dec21,1,7635703.story?coll=la-headlines-calendar&ctrack=1&cset=true "Taken in by a complete fake"]. ''Los Angeles Times''. Accessed December 24, 2007.</ref>

Greenhalgh was adept at obtaining and working in a wide variety of materials,<ref>[https://www.standard.co.uk/news/the-artful-codgers-pensioners-who-conned-british-museums-with-10m-forgeries-7300483.html "The artful codgers: pensioners who conned British museums with £10m forgeries"]. ''London Evening Standard''. November 16, 2007.</ref> and not only used a [[stoneware]] that fitted in well with what Gauguin demonstrably used, he managed to produce something "which had no obvious features to reveal it as a modern fake".<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> At 47 cm, it was modest, yet typically sized for a Gauguin. The gallery caption of ''The Faun'' read "unglazed stoneware with touches of gold [[gilding]]".<ref name="slide 2">Art Institute of Chicago. [https://web.archive.org/web/20070612125413/http://www.artic.edu/aic/exhibitions/vangogh/slideshow/slide_work02.html ''The Faun'' (slide 02)], in ''Slideshow: Van Gogh and Gauguin: The studio of the south''. Art Institute of Chicago. September 22, 2001. Archived from the original on June 12, 2007.</ref> Use of the gold gilding was deft; it was similar to investments Greenhalgh had made on previous forgeries. In 1991, for example, he is thought to have melted down genuine [[Argenteus|Roman silver coins]] when reconstructing the [[Risley Park Lanx]].<ref name=chadwick>Chadwick, Edward (November 17, 2007). [http://www.theboltonnews.co.uk/display.var.1840818.0.antiques_rogues_show_update_3.php "Antiques rogues show: update 3"]. ''The Bolton News''. Accessed November 30, 2007.</ref> Any anomalies in ''The Faun'' that were detected were explained away.<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake"/>

==Sold twice over==
In 1995, ''The Faun'' was sold at [[Sotheby's]] for £20,700.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> The Greenhalghs, who worked together as a family, had constructed a [[provenance]] based around Olive Greenhalgh (Shaun's mother), using her maiden name "Roscoe". She claimed to be a descendant of Roderick O'Conor,<ref name="nytimes.com"/> a friend of Gauguin's purported to have bought the sculpture at the 1917 exhibition, and known to have bought at least one other. Legitimising their ownership through inheritance was a typical ploy of the Greenhalghs, as was forging documents to go with it.<ref name=kelly>Kelly, James (November 16, 2007). [http://news.bbc.co.uk/2/hi/uk_news/7091435.stm "Fraudsters who resented the art market"]. BBC News. Accessed November 17, 2007.</ref> In this case, Olive produced a copy of the sale invoice.<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake"/>

There were no concerns about [[Authenticity in art|authenticity]]. As well as being well received by Sotheby's itself, ''The Faun'' was authenticated by the [[Wildenstein Index Number|Wildenstein Institute]] in Paris. Their [[catalogue raisonné]] had not yet been published when the sculpture was sold on 30 November, but the auction house had received a letter two weeks beforehand indicating ''The Faun's'' incorporation.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/>

The first buyers were experienced London [[art dealer]]s Howie and Pillar. They lived with it for years and described it as "a wonderful object".
When the [[curator]] for the Art Institute of Chicago, Douglas Druick, saw ''The Faun'' he was reportedly "intrigued"<ref name="nytimes.com"/> and "very keen to acquire it".<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> Subsequently, the Art Institute carried out their own research into the authenticity of the item and purchased it in 1997, for what was thought to be about $125,000. However, to this day, the Art Institute has refused to reveal actual details of the price it paid.<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake"/> What is known is that the purchase was funded, at least in part, by the Major Acquisitions Centennial Endowment<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> and is associated with the estate of Suzette Morton Davidson.<ref name="slide 2"/> At any rate, the Art Institute plans to seek compensation from Sotheby's.<ref name="Auto87-11">[http://www.artic.edu/sites/default/files/press_pdf/Gauguin_Statement.pdf "Art Institute's statement regarding Paul Gauguin's ''The Faun''"]. Art Institute of Chicago. Accessed December 24, 2007.</ref>

==The "good sculpture"==
Purchase of ''The Faun'' was proclaimed as a great success. Chief curator Douglas Druick declared it Gauguin's "first ceramic". In 2001, The Art Institute sculpture curator, Ian Wardropper, said it was one of the most important acquisitions in the last twenty years. ''The Faun'' was included in a publication of Chicago's "Notable Acquisitions". It was accepted by a specialist in Gauguin ceramics, Anne-Birgitte Fonsmark. The consensus of analysis was that the half-man half-goat fitted with Gauguin's known exploration of [[primitivism]], and various attempts were made to provide a detailed interpretation of ''The Faun's'' sexuality in terms of Gauguin's relationships. Druick noted  "the absence of the often flaunted sign of a faun’s [[virility]], resulting in an aura of [[impotence]]".<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> Even after it was exposed as a forgery, [[James Cuno]], the director of the Art Institute, still described it as "good sculpture".<ref name="nytimes.com"/>

==The "Van Gogh and Gauguin" exhibition==
On September 21, 2001, ''The Faun'' became part of a major exhibition, "Van Gogh and Gauguin: The Studio of the South". Organised as a joint venture between The Art Institute of Chicago and the van Gogh Museum in Amsterdam, the event ran for four months in Chicago before shifting to Amsterdam. Funding was unprecedented, with support from the Federal Council on the [[National Endowment for the Arts|Arts]] and the [[National Endowment for the Humanities|Humanities]], and a $1.5 million grant from the [[Ameritech|Ameritech Foundation]].<ref>[http://www.thefreelibrary.com/Art+Institute+Announces+Unprecedented+Support+from+Ameritech+For+Van...-a054078668 "Art Institute announces unprecedented support from Ameritech for Van Gogh-Gauguin exhibition"]. PR Newswire. March 11, 1999. Accessed September 3, 2012.</ref> The exhibition brought together works from "63 public and private collections around the world, including the U.S., Canada, Europe, Israel, Japan and Russia".<ref name="att.com">{{cite press release |url=http://www.att.com/gen/press-room?pid=4800&cdvn=news&newsarticleid=3061 |title=Ameritech Offers a Unique Canvas to Bring Works of van Gogh and Gauguin to Chicago's Sidewalks; Gallery 37 Artists to Paint Ameritech Manhole Covers Throughout the City to Celebrate Upcoming van Gogh and Gauguin Exhibition at The Art Institute of Chicago |url-status=deviated |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110608010310/http://www.att.com/gen/press-room?pid=4800&cdvn=news&newsarticleid=3061 |archive-date=8 June 2011 |work=[[AT&T]]}}</ref> It took years to prepare.<ref name="query.nytimes.com">[[Michael Kimmelman|Kimmelman, Michael]] (October 4, 2001). [https://query.nytimes.com/gst/fullpage.html?res=9C06E2DE1E3DF937A35753C1A9679C8B63 "Critic's notebook: irritation as inspiration"]. ''New York Times''. Accessed December 24, 2007.</ref> Joseph Harriss wrote in the ''[[Smithsonian (magazine)|Smithsonian]]'':
{{blockquote|New findings from the archives and technical research using microscopic study, [[radiography|x-radiography]], thread counts, and fiber- and paint-sample analysis have allowed curators to piece together an almost day-to-day picture of the ... collaboration [between Gauguin and van Gogh].<ref>Harriss, Joseph. [http://www.accessmylibrary.com/coms2/summary_0286-7324500_ITM "Strange Bedfellows"]. Smithsonian. December 1, 2001. Accessed September 3, 2012.</ref>}}
Promoters described the exhibition as "extraordinary"<ref name="att.com"/> and a "serious and very beautiful show."<ref name="query.nytimes.com"/> Art critic Suzanne Hoefaerkamp felt viewers were "unified by their experience of great art."<ref name="Studio of the South">Hoefaerkamp, Suzanne (January 16, 2002). "Studio of the South". ''The Christian Century'' '''119'''(2).</ref>

Of the 134 items on display, most were paintings, plus three [[Japanese prints]] by [[Hokusai]], [[Hiroshige]] and [[Ogata Kōrin|Korin]].<ref name="Auto87-14">[http://www.artic.edu/aic/exhibitions/vangogh/vg_list.html "List of works in the exhibition"]. Art Institute of Chicago. September 22, 2007. Accessed December 24, 2007.</ref> The focus of the exhibition, and the critics, was very much on the interplay between the paintings.<ref name="query.nytimes.com"/><ref name="Studio of the South"/> In fact, there were only seven sculptures, all by Gauguin. The others were ''Portrait Vase of Jeanne Schuffenecker'', ''Cleopatra Pot'', ''Leda and the Swan'', ''Self-portrait Jug'', ''Self-portrait Jar'', and ''Female Nude with Flower (known as Lust)''.<ref name="Auto87-14"/> The slideshow for the exhibition was arranged chronologically, so that ''The Faun'' (slide 02) could be clearly seen as Gauguin's first ceramic. Equally self-evident is how well the forgery fitted in thematically.

==Exposure and reaction==
In 2007, Shaun Greenhalgh was convicted for [[money laundering]], predominately over the ''[[Amarna Princess]]''. However, during the trial, the variety and number of his other forgeries were widely noted. Scotland Yard admitted that many were likely to be still undetected.<ref name=kelly/><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20110517065202/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/visual_arts/article2886205.ece "The £10m art collection that was forged by a family in their garden shed in Bolton"]. ''Times Online''. November 17, 2007. Archived from [https://web.archive.org/web/20110517065202/http://entertainment.timesonline.co.uk/tol/arts_and_entertainment/visual_arts/article2886205.ece the original] on May 17, 2011.</ref><ref>Ward, David (November 17, 2007). [https://www.theguardian.com/uk/2007/nov/17/artnews.art "How garden shed fakers fooled the art world"]. ''The Guardian''. Accessed November 17, 2007.</ref> Picking up on references to the Gauguin faun, ''[[The Art Newspaper]]'' launched its own investigation and tracked ''The Faun'' down to the Art Institute in Chicago.<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/>

The Art Institute was quick to emphasise, in a statement on its website, that the sculpture came with provenance from respected sources, and ''The Faun'' was "never a principal focus of the [Greenhalgh] investigation".<ref name="Auto87-11"/> Douglas Druick, the chief curator, described ''The Faun'' as "creative [and] well-researched". James Cuno, the director, said it was "a crafty concept".<ref name="theartnewspaper.com"/> According to Ian Wardropper, then the sculpture curator, the provenance was "completely believable".<ref name="Taken in by a complete fake"/> Melaine Clore from Sotheby's described ''The Faun'' as a once-in-a-decade forgery.<ref name="nytimes.com"/> On the process of obtaining artworks, Cuno added: "We make thousands of decisions like this annually. Once in a lifetime something like this happens."<ref>Blakely, Derrik (December 14, 2007). [http://www.truveo.com/Art-Institute-Discovers-Gauguin-Sculpture-Is-Fake/id/815459081 "Art Institute discovers Gauguin sculpture is fake (video)"] {{dead link|date=September 2012}}. CBS2. December 14, 2007. Accessed December 24, 2007. Quote at 1'40".</ref> However, other commentators speculate that as much as half of the art market is made up of forgeries.<ref>Sharp, Rob (December 10, 2007). [https://www.independent.co.uk/arts-entertainment/art/features/the-counterfeiters-inside-the-world-of-art-forgery-764032.html "The counterfeiters: Inside the world of art forgery"]. ''The Independent''. Accessed September 3, 2012.</ref>

In October 2007, ''The Faun'' was removed from Art Institute where it had been on permanent display as part of its [[Post-Impressionism|Post-Impressionist]] collection. It remained on the website as part of the "Studio of the South" exhibition slideshow until mid-December. Because Greenhalgh's trial finished before the sculpture was revealed as a forgery, it was not impounded by police, but the Art Institute was reportedly in discussion about compensation with Sotheby's and the private dealer.

A third former subgenus, ''[[Procapra]]'', includes three living species of Asian gazelles. Gazelles are known as swift animals. Some can run at bursts as high as {{Convert|60|mph|km/h|abbr=on|order=flip|sigfig=1}} or run at a sustained speed of {{Convert|30|mph|km/h|abbr=on|order=flip|sigfig=1}}."Gazelle". The Columbia Electronic Encyclopedia, 6th ed. 2007, Columbia University Press. Gazelles are found mostly in the deserts, grasslands, and [[savanna]]s of [[Africa]], but they are also found in [[Southwest Asia|southwest]] and [[central Asia]] and the [[Indian subcontinent]]. They tend to live in herds, and eat fine, easily digestible plants and leaves. Gazelles are relatively small antelopes, most standing {{convert|2|-|3.5|ft|cm|abbr=on|order=flip|-1}} high at the shoulder, and are generally [[Fawn (colour)|fawn-colored]]. The gazelle genera are ''Gazella'', ''Eudorcas'', and ''Nanger''. The [[Taxonomy (biology)|taxonomy]] of these genera is confused, and the classification of [[species]] and [[subspecies]] has been an unsettled issue. Currently, the genus ''Gazella'' is widely considered to contain about 10 species.{{Citation |title=The curious case of Gazella arabica | author=Eva Verena Bärmann|display-authors=etal | journal=Mammalian Biology - Zeitschrift für Säugetierkunde | year=2013 | volume=78 | issue=3 | pages=220–225 | doi=10.1016/j.mambio.2012.07.003| bibcode=2013MamBi..78..220B}} One species is extinct: the [[Queen of Sheba's gazelle]]. Most surviving gazelle species are considered [[threatened]] to varying degrees. Closely related to the true gazelles are the [[Goa (antelope)|Tibetan goa]], and [[Mongolian gazelle]]s (species of the genus ''Procapra''), the [[blackbuck]] of Asia, and the African [[springbok]]. One widely familiar gazelle is the African species [[Thomson's gazelle]] (''Eudorcas thomsonii''), sometimes referred to as a "tommie". It is around {{Convert|60|to|70|cm|in|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} in shoulder height and is coloured brown and white with a distinguishing black stripe. The males have long, often curved, horns. Like many other prey species, tommies exhibit a distinctive behaviour of [[stotting]] (running and jumping high before fleeing) when they are threatened by predators such as [[cheetah]]s, [[lion]]s, [[African wild dog]]s, [[crocodile]]s, [[hyena]]s, and [[leopard]]s. ==Etymology== [[Image:תמונה 1108.jpg|thumb|250px|Byzantine-era mosaic of gazelle in [[Caesarea (modern town)|Caesarea, Israel]]]] ''Gazelle'' is derived from [[French language|French]] ''gazelle'', [[Old French]] ''gazel'', probably via [[Old Spanish]] ''gacel'', probably from North African pronunciation of {{langx|ar|غزال}} ''{{Transliteration|ar|DIN|ġazāl}}'',{{Cite web |title=gazelle {{!}} Etymology, origin and meaning of gazelle by etymonline |url=https://www.etymonline.com/word/gazelle |access-date=2023-02-10 |website=www.etymonline.com |language=en}}{{Cite Skeat|gazelle|page=236}} [[Maghrebi Arabic|Maghrebi]] pronunciation ''{{Transliteration|ar|DIN|ġazēl}}''.{{cite web|url=https://www.cnrtl.fr/etymologie/gazelle|title=gazelle|website=CNRTL}} To Europe it first came to [[Old Spanish]] and [[Old French]], and then around 1600 the word entered the [[English language]].{{Cite web|title=Definition of GAZELLE|url=https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/gazelle|access-date=2023-02-23|website=www.merriam-webster.com|language=en}} The [[Arab people]] traditionally hunted the gazelle. Later appreciated for its grace, however, it became a symbol most commonly associated in [[Arabic]] literature with human beauty.{{cite book|title=Beauty in Arabic culture|first1=Doris|last1=Behrens-billAbouseif|edition=Illustrated|publisher=Markus Wiener Publishers|year=1999|isbn=978-1-55876-199-5|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=GQ2aFwUR3mgC&pg=PA53|page=53}}{{cite conference |author=Jokha Alharthi (PhD) |url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288181275|title=The Representation of the Beloved's Body in classical Arabic Poetry |conference=Scientific cooperations workshops on social sciences|location= Titanic Business Bayrampaşa- Istanbul |date=May 2015}} ==Species== {{Hatnote|For gazelle species by population, see [[List of even-toed ungulates by population]]}} The gazelles are divided into three genera and numerous species.{{cite web|title=Antilopinae|url=http://www.ultimateungulate.com/Cetartiodactyla/Antilopinae.html|access-date=2008-07-01}} {| class="wikitable sortable" |- ! Some examples include the [[Joof family]] of the [[Senegambia region]],[[Louis Diène Faye|Faye, Louis Diène]], ''Mort et naissance: le monde [[Serer people|Sereer]]'', Nouvelles Éditions africaines (1983), p. 74, {{ISBN|9782723608688}}{{Cite book|last=Gastellu|first=Jean-Marc|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=cc0xdPE35ngC|title=L'égalitarisme économique des Serer du Sénégal|date=1981|publisher=IRD Editions|isbn=978-2-7099-0591-6|language=fr|page=130}} the Bagananoa of [[Botswana]] in [[Southern Africa]] (said to be descended from the BaHurutshe),{{Cite book|last1=Chidester|first1=David|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RlHs4yC0eP0C&pg=PA341|title=African Traditional Religion in South Africa: An Annotated Bibliography: An Annotated Bibliography|last2=Kwenda|first2=Chirevo|last3=Petty|first3=Robert|last4=Tobler|first4=Judy|last5=Wratten|first5=Darrel|date=1997-08-07|publisher=ABC-CLIO|isbn=978-0-313-03225-7|language=en|page=341}} and the Eraraka (or Erarak) clan of [[Uganda]].{{cite book|author=Roscoe, John|title=The Northern Bantu: An Account of Some Central African Tribes of the Uganda Protectorate|publisher= The University Press |year=1915 |page= 262}} As is common in many African societies, it is forbidden for the Joof or Eraraka to kill or touch the family totem. === Poetry === One of the traditional themes of Arabic love poetry involves comparing the gazelle with the beloved, and linguists theorize ''[[ghazal]]'', the word for love poetry in Arabic, is related to the word for gazelle.{{cite book|title=Muqarnas: An Annual on the Visual Culture of the Islamic World|first1=Gülru|last1=Necipoğlu|editor=Gülru Necipoğlu|edition=Illustrated|publisher=BRILL|year=1997|isbn=978-90-04-10872-1|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=s6MN2T9cXNEC&pg=PA15}} The [[Caliph]] [[Abd al-Malik ibn Marwan|Abd al-Malik]] (646–705) freed a gazelle that he had captured because of her resemblance to his beloved: {{center| O likeness of [[Layla and Majnun|Layla]], never fear!
For I am your friend, today, O wild gazelle!
Then I say, after freeing her from her fetters:
You are free for the sake of Layla, for ever! }} The theme is found in the ancient Hebrew [[Song of Songs]]. (8:14) {{center| Come away, my beloved,
and be like a gazelle
or like a young stag
on the spice-laden mountains. }} ==Gallery== File:Grants Gazelle Gazella granti in Tanzania 2645 Nevit.jpg|[[Grant's gazelle]] (male) File:Gazella dama mhorr 2.jpg|[[Dama Gazelle|Mhorr gazelle]] File:Cuvier's Gazelle.jpg|[[Cuvier's gazelle]] (female) File:Gazella thomsonii - Disney's Animal Kingdom Lodge, Orlando, Florida, USA - 20100916.jpg|[[Thomson's gazelle]] (male) File:Gazella spekei (Speke's Gazelle).jpg|[[Speke's gazelle]] (female) File:Group of Gazella subgutturosa.JPG|[[Goitered gazelle]] (females and young) File:Chinkara.jpg|[[Chinkara]] (female) File:Gazella-dorcas.jpg|[[Dorcas gazelle]] (female) File:Gazella rufifrons AB.jpg|[[Red-fronted gazelle]] File:Gazella gazella.jpg|[[Mountain gazelle]] (male) File:GazellaSoemmerringiWolf.jpg|[[Soemmerring's gazelle]] (females) File:Slender-horned gazelle (Cincinnati Zoo).jpg|[[Slender-horned gazelle]] (male) File:Granada Alhambra gazelle Poterie 9019.JPG|Gazelles on one of the [[Alhambra vases|vases]] made for the [[Alhambra]] palace ==References== {{sister project links|auto=yes}} {{Reflist|30em}} {{Artiodactyla|R.5}} {{Taxonbar|from=Q190858}} {{Authority control}} [[Category:Gazella| ]] [[Category:Antilopinae]] [[Category:Extant Pliocene first appearances]] [[Category:Mammals of Africa]] [[Category:Mammals of Asia]] [[Category:Taxa named by Henri Marie Ducrotay de Blainville]]
